name: A Two-Concept Holonomy Shore Is an Active Edge
statement: If a passive shore $S$ on a directed lower holonomy cycle has two concepts, then $S=\{r,o\}$ with $r$ a lower active root and $o$ a non-root common owner, and $ro$ is an active edge.
proof: The shore-root theorem supplies $r$, while the predecessor blocker and common-owner depth transfer supply $o\notin R$. The ample gate $L\cup S$ and its first prefix $L\cup\{r\}$ are ample, whereas $L\cup\{o\}$ is not. If $r$ and $o$ were nonadjacent, a blocker in $L$ for adding $o$ would survive after adding $r$, contradicting ampleness of the gate by the one-concept colon criterion.
